subject: Suspicious trial issuance — multiple signups from gearworks.ai
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious: auto-issued trials to gearworks.ai cluster (alert)

Hi team,

Payment ops flagged a batch of self-serve trial credit issuances that all map back to @gearworks.ai addresses over the past 3 hours. Patterns look like: same UA string, similar device_fingerprint, and two IPs that shift through a small range (listed in attachment).

Quick summary:
- 27 new accounts created in last 3h
- 24 received automatic trial credits (self-serve flow)
- Commonalities: email domain gearworks.ai, rotational IPs within 3.14.22.x/28 and 18.201.7.x/29, repeated signup payload fields

I attached signup_payload.json and a short IP list (ip_trace.log). My hypothesis: either an org-wide signup using a shared alias or an automated script.

What do you want me to do with the outstanding issuances (hold/rollback)? I can pause auto-issuance for the domain and queue a manual review.

Thanks,
Dev
Engineering Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: signup_payload.json (text), ip_trace.log (text)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious: auto-issued trials to gearworks.ai cluster (alert)

Thanks Dev — good catch.

My thinking: hold any further auto-issuance for gearworks.ai and do not revoke already-issued credits until we validate. If it looks automated, we should roll back the 24 issuances and flag the accounts for manual verification.

Marissa, can you pull the HubSpot / signup metadata and check if GearWorks appears as an expected account (sales touch, contact, PO requests)? If not, we should contact the main ops email and request confirmation before any credits are re-enabled.

Also looping security on SEC-2143 (I created the ticket) and will keep legal in the loop if rollback affects customers.

—Mateo
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious: auto-issued trials to gearworks.ai cluster (alert)

On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 09:12 AM Dev Patel wrote:
> Payment ops flagged a batch of self-serve trial credit issuances that all map back to @gearworks.ai addresses over the past 3 hours.

I pulled the HubSpot trace and cross-checked logs. Findings:
- HubSpot company record: GearWorks Inc. (company id 99873) — no recent sales touches or demo requests logged in the past 6 months.
- The signup payloads show the same utm_source and identical referral token — likely one origin.
- Device fingerprints show very low entropy (same canvas/hash) across accounts.
- IPs reverse-resolve to cloud provider hostnames (likely rented infra).

Recommended next steps:
1) Pause auto-issuance for gearworks.ai domain and mark the 24 accounts as "pending verification" (do not charge nor allow model calls beyond sandbox level).
2) Send a short verification email to ops@gearworks.ai requesting: org email alias confirmation OR a signed PO if they expect credits.
3) If no response in 48 hours, revoke credits and blacklist or rate-limit further signups from the IP ranges and UA.

I attached ip_trace.log with the IP clusters.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales (Americas)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ip_trace.log (text)
From: Nina Park <nina.park@gearworks.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@gearworks.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:15:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious: auto-issued trials to gearworks.ai cluster (alert)

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks for the heads up — I work on IT at GearWorks. We did run a company-wide evaluation last week where several team leads signed up to try Redwood for different feature teams. The emails are legitimate aliases we create for sandbox use (e.g., infra-team@gearworks.ai, ml-ops@gearworks.ai). We use dynamic cloud instances for testing, so the IP behavior you flagged makes sense for our internal infra.

What we can provide:
- A short confirmation email from our CTO, Samir Rao.
- A PO for evaluation credits if you prefer (I can route this internally).

Please advise on next steps; we don't want legitimate evaluation access revoked unexpectedly.

Best,
Nina Park
IT Operations
GearWorks Inc.
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@gearworks.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious: auto-issued trials to gearworks.ai cluster (alert)

Thanks Nina — appreciate the quick response and context.

We want to avoid interrupting legitimate evals while protecting platform credits from abuse. Proposed plan:
- We will mark the 24 accounts as limited (sandbox usage only) while we verify.
- Please have Samir Rao (CTO) reply to this thread confirming the evaluation and list the team aliases that should keep full access, or provide a single PO/confirmation email from an exec. That will let us re-enable credits immediately for the verified aliases.
- If we do not receive confirmation within 48 hours, we will revoke the trial credits and rate-limit future signups from the IP ranges indicated.

Internal: Dev, please pause auto-issuance for gearworks.ai and add an allowlist task to SEC-2143 if we get a CTO confirmation. Marissa, I'll pick this up on the sales side if they send a PO.

Mateo
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
